page.overview:
Who is Ancalagon The Black?

Ancalagon, also known as Anddraca, the Great Dragon of Morgoth, the Black Dragon, or the Black, was the "greatest of the winged dragons of Morgoth" and "mightiest of the dragon-host" during the War of Wrath. He was bred by Morgoth during the First Age and possibly was the largest winged dragon to have ever existed in Middle-earth.

During the late First Age, the Wise-woman Andreth, of the Edain, once made a prophecy "that Túrin" would return before leaving the Circles of the World and slay Ancalagon during the Last Battle., is untold.

After Eärendil made his journey to Valinor to convince the Valar to overthrow Morgoth and rescue the overmatched and defeated Elves and Edain, the Host of Valinor made war upon Morgoth and destroyed his armies during the War of Wrath.

In the year 587, Morgoth unleashed his last and greatest weapon; a fleet of winged dragons, which he had been hiding in Angband. They were "winged with steel" and Ancalagon was among them. Their onslaught was so terrible that the armies of the Valar were driven back to Dor-nu-Fauglith from the gates of Angband, and their coming was said to have been accompanied by great thunderbolts, lightning, and fire storms. But Eärendil came out of the West in his blessed ship Vingilot, accompanied by "a myriad" of "all the great birds of heaven" led by their captain, Thorondor, an Eagle. The Eagles and Eärendil dueled with Ancalagon and the other dragons for a day and a night. Before the next sunrise, Eärendil was victorious "and overthrew Ancalagon", casting him down "upon the towers of Thangorodrim", destroying them in his fall. The death of Ancalagon marked the end of Morgoth's final resistance.
